content.comment_body: Can someone clarify if and when [product_name] will be compatible with Windows 7? I know it's working with other versions, but for Windows 7 there's a small issue. Thanks!

Hello [user_name], It's helpful to use the forum search function. I found three related threads which might help: [product_name] 6.1, [product_name] Version 4 in Windows 7, and Windows 7 x64bit with [product_name] v5.0. Best regards, [user_name]

We're all waiting for proper support... Microsoft really changed things with Windows 7, so it's understandable [product_name] isn't ready yet. Since [product_name] relies on Java, official support only comes after thorough system testing, which might take months! Maybe next year we'll see Windows 7 compatibility with the expected new [product_name] release. Some users have had partial success using compatibility modes, dual-boot, or virtual machines, but most problems come from outdated USB cable drivers. These need updating for Windows 7 first. Quite frustrating for everyone with newer PCs!

Today I found a method to get [product_name] running on Windows 7-64 Pro English. Here's what worked: First, remove all Java versions from your notebook (both x86 and x64) using the control panel. Then, download the latest x64 Java from the official website and install it as administrator. Confirm the installation by checking the Java Control Panel for the correct version. Back up your [product_name] projects, uninstall the program, and restart Windows. After reboot, insert your [product_name] CD (mine was v6.1), skip autorun, and manually run 'setup.bat' from the installation folder as administrator. After installation, check all functions and update to the latest [product_name] version. The only issue I noticed is missing icons when browsing in the open menu; however, labels still display when you hover. No more freezing when saving or opening files. Hope this helps.
Hi [user_name], How did you install the USB cable drivers? This seems to be where a lot of users are having trouble—the driver isn't officially supported for Windows 7 yet. Thanks!

USB drivers were installed automatically by Windows using the hardware compatibility publisher driver update. When I connected the cable, the usual wizard appeared: found new hardware, searched the internet, and installed the driver automatically. The driver was signed by MWHCP, published by Silicon Labs, version 5.4.29.0 (dated 03/02/2010). I can't upload a screenshot showing [product_name] running online mode and the device manager tab with the driver, but you can send a message with your email and I'll forward it, or a moderator can post it.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report compatibility issues running [product_name] on Windows 7, especially with 64-bit systems and USB driver support. The switch to Windows 7 has led to some missing features or icons, but core functions can often be restored with manual workarounds. The primary frustration is a lack of official Windows 7 support, leading to confusion and the need for user-devised fixes.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to work seamlessly with Windows 7, without missing features, UI problems, crashes, or workaround requirements. They also expect native USB driver support for easy connectivity.
